title: Motor Position Rule Checker
description: Ten order lines in a fixed order; for each the learner judges Standard, Allowed with condition or Not allowed and, for Not allowed, picks the correction (one scored attempt, mastery 8 of 10 on the first attempt). After Check a schematic sketch shows the motor in the correct position with the FanPedia rule.
creator: Twin City Fan

inline motor positions A to H

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Motor position rules for arrangement variants
learningObjectives: The learner will apply FanPedia's motor position rules to ten order lines, judging each as standard, allowed with a condition, or not allowed, and stating the correct position or conduit box when the line is wrong.
prerequisites: plenum positions S, O and TC
inline motor positions A to H

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); selections and verdicts announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗/→ glyphs on the verdict buttons and solid/dashed feedback borders pair with colour; blocked inline positions are dashed and carry ✗; keys 1-3 choose a verdict, Not allowed moves focus to the Fix list, Enter checks or goes on.

Fix
controls.purpose: For Not allowed: choose the correction

controls.label: Next line / Finish
controls.purpose: Go to the next line; after line 10, show the summary (Enter)

rules: Verdict and correction come from FP.codes.checkMotorLine (FanPedia pp. 52, 53, 55, 56).
Standard = the pairing FanPedia lists as standard; Allowed with condition = a listed option tied to a stated condition; Not allowed = a pairing FanPedia excludes.
The correction is scored only when the verdict is Not allowed; an item counts when both are right.
Ten lines in a fixed order, one scored attempt each; mastery 8 of 10 on the first attempt.
assumptions: The clearance situation in item 3 is illustrative.
limitations: Sketches are schematic and not to scale; swing side is shown as a label only.

sources: FanPedia: The Fan & Blower Encyclopedia, pp. 52, 53, 55 and 56

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Judge an order line against the rule, then correct it, as an order desk does
keyQuestions: Which motor position system does this arrangement use?
Is the pairing the standard, an option with a condition, or excluded?
If excluded, what is the smallest change that makes it ship?
commonMisconceptions: L and R are free choices on every pedestal-mounted motor.
A 9SS can take either motor position on either swing.
Arrangement 10 has a motor position to choose.
A floor mounted inline fan can take any of A to H.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'First-attempt score: n of 10'; mastery is 8 of 10 on the first attempt.
Summary list of missed lines with their rules.
